<page-num>74</page-num>
<header>APPENDIX TO</header>

### To find what Planet rules any *Hour* of the *Day* by the *Table No. III.*

Please note that astrological hours are governed by the movement of the sun in both summer and winter. The period of time between sunrise and sunset is divided into twelve equal parts; the first six parts contain the hours before noon, and the remaining six contain the hours after noon. Similarly, the period from sunset until sunrise is also divided into twelve parts. These hours are "unequal"—meaning they may be longer or shorter than sixty minutes—depending on how far the sun has moved from the signs of Aries (♈) or Libra (♎), as shown by the examples in the previous Table.

Ancient traditions assigned the seven planets to preside over the seven days of the week, and each planet rules the first hour of its corresponding day, as can be seen in the Table. For instance, the first planetary hour of Sunday is the Sun, the second is Venus, and so on. The first planetary hour of Monday is the Moon, the second is Saturn; the same pattern applies to the other days of the week.

The use of these Tables is clear upon simple inspection; they require no calculation, and even a person of modest ability will be able to understand them. The reason for presenting them as tables is that previous Herbals <note>Books describing the medicinal properties and lore of plants.</note>—which discuss the power of planetary influence <term>planetary influx</term> and the necessity of gathering herbs for medical use under the planet that principally governs them—failed to provide any rule for an herbalist <note>original: herbarist</note> to know when those planetary hours actually occur. Without this, one could not know the proper time to harvest them. This deficiency has not only caused much frustration for many medical practitioners but has also hindered the progress of healing. Many disorders have been deemed incurable simply because doctors lacked the precision necessary to achieve a perfect cure.

These Tables are designed so that one can easily identify those ideal times when a human—who possesses a rational soul originating from the divine center—can expand their awareness into the realm of nature. By doing so, one can identify the exact hour not only to gather herbs and roots but also to administer them at a time that corresponds to their nature. This helps to expel from the patient the disease <term>offending matter</term> that robs them of the invaluable blessing of health. However, since I do not intend this to be a full academic treatise, but rather a small part of the *Key to Physic* <note>A guide to the art of medicine.</note>, I will skip further observations on the ebb and flow of earthly <term>sublunary</term> virtues in worldly <term>terrene</term> things. Truth requires few words to recommend it and will prove itself through trial. These Tables, and the rest of this little "Key," will demonstrate to the suffering patient or the compassionate physician that they are the legitimate result of TRUTH and EXPERIENCE.

<meta>This page provides practical examples of how to use the astrological tables introduced on the previous page. These calculations allowed herbalists to determine the precise "planetary hour" for gathering medicinal plants, ensuring they were harvested under the correct celestial influence.</meta>

<page-num>75</page-num>
<header>CULPEPER’S BRITISH HERBAL. 75</header>

### EXAMPLE I.

To find the planetary hour on Sunday, April 22, 1792, at half past ten o’clock in the morning: I examine the *Ephemeris* <term>Ephemeris</term> <note>A book or table providing the daily positions of the sun, moon, and planets.</note> to see what degree the Sun is in, and I find that on that day at noon, it is at three degrees of the sign Taurus (♉). Using this degree, I look at Table No. I and seek three degrees of Taurus in the first column. By following the row across to the seventh column, I find 10:49 AM. By looking at the top of the Table, this shows me that the fifth planetary hour would finish at forty-nine minutes past ten o'clock in the morning. Now I refer to the previous column and find that the fifth planetary hour began at thirty-seven minutes past nine o'clock. Since the time I started with was 10:30 AM, and that falls between 9:37 AM and 10:49 AM, it is proven to be the fifth planetary hour. To know which planet ruled this hour, I look at Table No. III. Counting down the planets in the first column under the heading "Sunday," I find the fifth planetary hour on that day is ruled by **Saturn**. If it had been on a Monday, the fifth planetary hour would have been the **Sun**; on a Tuesday, it would have been the **Moon**; on a Wednesday, **Mars**; and so on. By following this rule, the planetary hour for any day of the week may be found.

### EXAMPLE II.

Suppose we want to find the hour of **Venus** on Saturday, January 19, 1793. I look into the *Ephemeris* and find that the Sun at noon on that day is at 0 degrees of Aquarius (♒) <note>original: Aquaries</note>. I look at the Table marked No. III, and in the column of planetary hours under Saturday, I find that the fifth hour is ruled by **Venus**. Now, as the Sun is at 0 degrees of Aquarius, I go to Table No. II. In the right-hand column for 0 degrees Aquarius, and in the ninth column on the left hand, I find that the planetary hour of Venus began at twenty minutes past eleven o'clock and continued until noon on that day.

Such was the method of practice when nature alone was consulted and the goal was truly to effect a cure without focusing on profit. In those days, disease was little known, and people lived to a good old age.

## GENERAL DIRECTIONS TO THE BINDER

Let the plates <note>Engraved illustrations.</note> belonging to the **APPENDIX** be placed as nearly opposite to the description of each plant as circumstances will allow. Observe never to place two illustrations together, but to turn over the next leaf so as to have one leaf of printed text between them.

### DIRECTIONS FOR BINDING THE KEY AND CULPEPER TOGETHER

Let the **APPENDIX** be placed at the end of **CULPEPER'S BRITISH HERBAL**, which will complete the first volume. At the end of the **MEDICAL PART of CULPEPER**, add the **KEY TO MEDICINE** <note>original: "KEY TO PHYSIC"; "Physic" was the standard term for the art of healing and medicine.</note>, etc., which will divide them into two uniform volumes and make the whole subject complete. These are to be labeled: **Dr. SIBLY'S FAMILY PHYSICIAN**.

### DIRECTIONS FOR BINDING Dr. SIBLY'S WORKS IN FOUR VOLUMES

Let the sixty installments <note>original: "Numbers"; books were often sold in weekly or monthly parts before being bound.</note> of the *Occult Sciences* be divided into two volumes, and add the two volumes mentioned above to them, making four volumes in total. They are to have two labels on the spine in the following order: **The WORKS of Dr. SIBLY** is to be the general title of each volume. Then, the specific titles are to be added:
*   Under **Vol. I**: **DOCTRINE of the STARS**.
*   Under **Vol. II**: **CALCULATION of NATIVITIES** <note>The practice of casting astrological birth charts.</note>.
*   Under **Vol. III**: **BRITISH HERBAL**.
*   Under **Vol. IV**: **FAMILY PHYSICIAN**.

Place the portrait of Dr. Sibly at the beginning of the first volume. The frontispiece <note>An illustration facing the title page.</note> of the *Occult Sciences* should face the second volume. The portrait of Culpeper should be in the third volume, and the frontispiece of the *Key* in the fourth volume.

A general title page for each volume of Dr. Sibly's works, to be placed before the frontispieces, may be obtained free of charge <note>original: "gratis"</note> by those who have purchased the entire series in installments and wish to bind them uniformly. These are available by applying to the publishers.

->END OF THE APPENDIX.<-
